title: TMC paid little-known company Rs 160 crore to buy a jet & helicopter: ED
content: 'Paid Another Rs 187Cr As Rent But Didn't Utilise Minimum Guaranteed Hours, Chartered Others For Rs 149Cr'

title: Ronaldo drops bombshell retirement hint, reveals plans for life after football
content: Cristiano Ronaldo has suggested the 2026-27 season could be the final year of his playing career, saying he wants to leave a “spectacular legacy”. The 41-year-old remains contracted to Al Nassr until June 2027 and has begun planning life after football, including spending more time with family, travelling and playing padel.

title: MacKenzie Scott helped abolish $40B in medical debt; how mechanics work
content: MacKenzie Scott's donations have enabled medical debt abolition across America. Her model allows acquiring debt at low costs and then forgiving it. This approach has inspired other billionaires to contribute millions to similar causes. While philanthropic efforts are scaling, policy reforms for medical debt remain stalled. Scott's work highlights immediate relief possibilities and the need for systemic change.

title: 'Awarapan 2' beats 'Batwara 1947' on day 3; nears Rs 100 crore
content: Awarapan 2 has made a remarkable impact, surpassing the lifetime earnings of its predecessor on its very first day. Thanks to the Independence Day weekend boost, it attracted impressive ticket sales. The strong box office performance in its opening weekend has already labeled it a success, achieving a rapid affirmation of its financial viability.

title: Exam-conducting body NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET test for 3 subjects
content: National Testing Agency acknowledged extensive errors in UGC-NET English, Commerce, and Sociology papers. Fresh examinations for these three subjects have been ordered by the agency. These re-tests are scheduled to take place on September 9 and 10. The decision came after multiple complaints regarding factual and typographical errors were received. Results for the other 84 subjects will be declared as scheduled.

title: US immigration authority: These forms will be rejected from September 15
content: USCIS will introduce new editions of immigration forms I-539 and I-765. These revised forms will be effective starting September 15, 2026. Applications submitted using older forms after this date will be rejected. This change aligns with a recently published immigration rule. USCIS emphasizes there will be no grace period for this form update.

title: CM Vijay condemns killing of 3 Tamil farmers in Karnataka; Stalin seeks judicial probe
content: Political leaders across Tamil Nadu have expressed outrage over the tragic killing of three farmers by Karnataka forest officials. Former Chief Minister M K Stalin has called for a judicial inquiry and demanded compensation for the bereaved families. He has also asked the Tamil Nadu government to publicly denounce Karnataka's actions.

title: Lynne Cox: Channel record at 15, swam Alaska to USSR in 38°F water at 30
content: In 1987, endurance swimmer Lynne Cox made waves by crossing the Bering Strait, swimming from Alaska to Soviet territory during a tense Cold War period. This monumental swim was more than a personal triumph; it represented a bridge of peace and understanding between two divided nations. Her bravery earned accolades from leaders in both the US and the Soviet Union, emphasizing the potential for cooperation in the Bering Strait region.

title: Hawaii’s 1905 mosquitofish import now linked to native species decline
content: The introduction of mosquitofish in Hawaii has dramatically affected the ecosystem, leading to notable declines in native aquatic insects. These invasive fish fiercely prey on local species, disrupting food chains. The native damselflies, unprepared for such predation, are particularly vulnerable, seeing their populations plummet. Additionally, mosquitofish compete with endemic fish and crustaceans for limited food resources, complicating control efforts due to intricate waterways and their fast breeding habits.

title: Elon Musk makes a promise to employees at townhall
content: SpaceX aims to enhance its AI model Grok by integrating insights from its workforce. Elon Musk envisions this initiative as a means to embed human values deeply into the AI's framework. Employees are not only invited to enhance the internal AI systems but are also inspired to share their expertise.

title: Brittany Mahomes explains why female athletes deserve more recognition
content: Brittany Mahomes has made her support for women’s sports clear while celebrating the launch of KC Current Studios. The former soccer player and Kansas City Current co-owner emphasized the impact sports can have beyond competition, including confidence, friendship and inspiration for young people. Her comments come amid wider debates surrounding women’s sports, though she focused on celebrating female athletes and ensuring their stories receive greater attention and recognition.

title: How fatherhood and his daughters changed Dak Prescott’s outlook on life
content: Dak Prescott’s journey into fatherhood has transformed how he views life, time and legacy. The Dallas Cowboys quarterback now looks beyond football and wants to experience every stage of his children’s lives, including seeing the families they may build someday. His perspective reflects the powerful impact of becoming a parent, especially after losing his own mother. For Prescott, success is no longer measured only by achievements, but by being present for family.

title: Why NHL players tape their sticks and how it improves puck control
content: NHL players tape their sticks for reasons that go way beyond hockey tradition. The tape changes the feel of the blade on the puck, helps prevent ice buildup, protects equipment and gives players a customized grip. From Connor McDavid to other NHL stars, individual tape jobs can be a reflection of playing style, comfort, visual preference, and well-established pregame routines.

title: From burnt cash to possibly first impeachment: Justice Varma saga explained
content: Justice Yashwant Varma's residence was engulfed in flames, leading to the shocking discovery of burnt currency notes. A subsequent parliamentary inquiry confirmed serious charges against him, prompting his resignation. The Centre's pursuit of impeachment aims to set a strong precedential framework for judicial accountability. This case also poses critical questions about the interplay between a judge's resignation and ongoing disciplinary proceedings, potentially impacting future cases of judicial misconduct.

title: ‘Rankings don’t matter’: Pakistan captain’s bold India warning ahead of WC clash
content: Captain Abu Bakar Mahmood of Pakistan dismisses the importance of rankings as his team gears up for the high-stakes match against India. He believes that the actual performance will determine the winner on the field. After ten years without a win against their fiercest opponents, Pakistan are eager to advance to the World Cup quarterfinals, relying on a blend of youthful energy and seasoned leadership to reclaim their legacy.

title: What happened to MLB legend Tommy John? Baseball icon dies at 83 after 26-year career
content: What happened to Tommy John? The MLB legend died peacefully at 83 at his Florida home, surrounded by his family. Days earlier, he had been in hospice care and shared a farewell message with Yankees fans. John finished his 26-year career with 288 wins, but his greatest legacy came from returning to baseball after groundbreaking elbow surgery.

title: Gaza peace plan: 8 nations condemn Israel's rejection of US roadmap
content: Several nations condemned Israel's rejection of the Gaza peace process proposal.  This move seriously undermines collective efforts to achieve lasting peace and stability.  The roadmap, accepted by Palestinian factions, was a culmination of intensive mediation efforts.  Israel insists Hamas must be disarmed before any troop withdrawal occurs.  The countries urged the US to compel Israel to fully comply with the plan.

title: 'He said pistol was unloaded': Injured staff on Varanasi airport firing incident
content: Two cargo screeners were injured when a passenger's pistol accidentally discharged during security checks. The passenger claimed the weapon was unloaded before he pressed the trigger to show them. One screener sustained an injury to his left hand, while the other was hit in both legs. The incident occurred at Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport while boarding a flight to Mumbai.

title: ‘Clearly, there’s something wrong’: Gavaskar questions India’s fitness methods
content: Sunil Gavaskar, the legendary former captain, raises concerns regarding the fitness and training methodologies of the Indian cricket team. He points out that the spate of hamstring injuries suggests flaws in the existing training strategies. Furthermore, Gavaskar questions the rationale behind limiting bowlers' net sessions in the name of biomechanics, insisting that match fitness should take priority over purely gym-focused conditioning.

title: 'Stay away from politics': TMC leader Asish Banerjee's suicide note surfaces
content: Former Trinamool Congress MLA Asish Banerjee was found dead at his party office. A suicide note was discovered, which reportedly mentioned his political journey. Banerjee had served as a five-time MLA and held ministerial portfolios. He stepped down from a party committee after losing his seat. His body was taken for a post-mortem examination.

title: Arsenal’s Calafiori sets 118-year record with fastest-ever Community Shield goal
content: Riccardo Calafiori scored after just 23 seconds against Manchester City to give Arsenal a record-breaking start in the 2026 Community Shield. His strike became the fastest goal in the competition’s 118-year history, beating Liverpool legend Gary McAllister’s previous Cardiff record. Arsenal then doubled their advantage through Kai Havertz, giving Mikel Arteta’s side an impressive opening to the season.

title: ‘Rahul, Hemant are dead’: Jharkhand protester performs ‘funeral’, shaves head
content: The protest by students and job aspirants over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the protesters, under the banner of JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accusing the ruling JMM-Congress alliance of failing to take “concrete action” on their demands. They have also announced plans to gherao Soren's residence in Ranchi on August 20 and demanded his resignation.

title: IND vs SL: The ninety minutes! Moving day comes early in gloomy Galle
content: A rain-hit Day 2 in Galle turned into a frantic 90 minutes as Sri Lanka's bowlers struck in quick succession, dismissing India's overnight batters and bringing the hosts back into the contest. Devdutt Padikkal's 167 and a crucial lower-order stand kept India in control, but the pitch is beginning to offer the turn and bounce expected in Galle.

title: Rs 6,400-crore IPO rush: 7 companies set to tap primary market next week
content: The IPO market anticipates a busy week with seven companies planning public offerings. These upcoming issues aim to collectively raise more than Rs 6,400 crore from investors. Horizon Industrial Parks and Lalithaa Jewellery Mart will launch their initial public offerings on August 17. Shankesh Jewellers and Sunshine Pictures are scheduled to open their issues on August 18.

title: ‘Unwanted record’: Ex-captain stunned after bizarre blunder by Pak at World Cup
content: Pakistan's hockey captain received a green card after gear was forgotten. This incident occurred during their opening World Cup match against England. The team failed to produce necessary protective equipment for a penalty corner. Former captain Salman Akbar criticised the lack of preparation and organisation. This lapse raises serious questions about the team's readiness for major events.

title: Groundwater that glows yellow-green in U.P.

title: 22,000 lawyers on Kerala’s bar council rolls unaccounted for
content: There are around 81,000 lawyers on the rolls of Bar Council of Kerala, of whom only 27,000 have certificates of practice that is mandatory of practising law. The certificates of around 25,000 lawyers are pending with various varsities for verification

title: Three arrested after Bengal CJP volunteer’s father dies in attack

title: Many initiatives in the pipeline to transform tourism sector in Tamil Nadu, say Ministers
content: River tourism to be promoted by connecting the Cauvery and the Thamirabarani; government considering giving free travel facilities for senior citizens to make tourism inclusive and accessible

title: JNU Vice-Chancellor terms allegations of irregularities in recruitment a ‘malicious campaign’
content: Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit says there is no evidence. JNU administration says disgruntled left-leaning JNUTA figures are behind the 'political campaign’ to embarrass the varsity and the Centre, in the wake of defeats in the Delhi HC involving two ‘urban Naxal’ cases

title: Why the Visakhapatnam airport shut, and what still flies from INS Dega
content: The 10.45 p.m. IndiGo to Delhi was the final scheduled service from the civil enclave at INS Dega. From 12.01 a.m. on Monday, every airline flight moves to Bhogapuram, and the code VTZ moves with them

title: Traffic around KBR Park goes one-way with 10 U-turn points and 13 exits from August 18
content: The lane-change and U-turn points are located at TG Study Circle, BRS Bhavan, Omega Hospital, Jana Reddy, Apollo Cradle, Taj Mahal, Phoenix Building, Road No. 65, Mantri Towers and Cream Stone.

title: "One Family One Ticket" Row Grows As BJP's Ravneet Bittu Targets Congress
content: The issue has intensified the ongoing political tussle between Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring and Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa.

content: The incident took place in the Rudha Dhamrua village in Ambedkarnagar. The victim, Indravati, used to live alone.

content: In a letter on Saturday, students and alumni of NLSIU said they stood in "unconditional solidarity" with their counterparts at NALSAR and criticised both the BCI chairman's conduct and the CJI's proposed participation in their own convocation.

content: They were among the estimated 5,000 to 8,000 who remain in Ceuta after the mass border crossing two weeks ago that saw over 72,000 people surge into the tiny territory of about 80,000.

title: Trump Envoy Meets Hamas Leaders Over Gaza Plan, Will See Netanyahu Next
content: The talks aim to salvage the new 15-point, US-backed road map for Hamas to disarm in Gaza and Israel to withdraw from the Palestinian territory shattered by war.

content: Local news outlets reported that Police Chief Lawrence Weathers said two children, aged 4 and 14, were among those shot at Charles Young Park in downtown Lexington.

title: "Disaster": 4 Renaissance-Era Paintings Stolen From Italian Museum
content: The thieves bypassed alarm and security systems on Saturday evening at the MuMe museum to make off with three of the five surviving panels of the San Gregorio Polyptych, dated to 1473.

title: Jharkhand Government Invites Student Protesters For Fresh Talks On Monday
content: The decision came after the Sub-Divisional Officer and ADM, Law and Order held a meeting with the students at the Jaipal Singh Munda Stadium here, the protest site.

content: Iran's nuclear programme has drawn international scrutiny for three decades, though Tehran insists it is for civilian purposes only.

content: "Amritsar Rural Police averts a terror plot targeting a police establishment and recovers an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) weighing 690 grams, along with an electronic detonator, battery, timer and iron box," Punjab Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav said in a post on X.

title: Chaos In Delhi Metro After Paramilitary Official Allegedly Takes Woman's Pic
content: The purported video of the incident that went viral shows Delhi Metro passengers confronting the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel, who initially denied taking the photos.

title: 400 Noida Families Don't Have Water. Children Scrape Leaked Pipe For Drops
content: Residents of Valmiki Basti in Sector 78 have been facing a water shortage for close to a month. With no supply, people were forced to collect water from a leak in a Gangajal pipeline running beneath a nearby drain.

title: Harsimrat Kaur Demands Anti-Terror Probe Into Sukhbir Badal Attack
content: Harsimrat Badal said the latest attack in Nanded and the December 4, 2024 attack on Sukhbir Badal at Sri Darbar Sahib could not be treated as isolated incidents.

content: Iranian Army chief Amir Hatami announced the $30,000 bounty to capture soldiers, saying that the plan had been drawn up after a "large number of requests" to participate, according to a report.

title: "If Any Indian Feels...": Kiren Rijiju Clarifies PM's "Dimangi Naxal" Remark
content: The Congress used to sing Vande Mataram in full and now they only sing the party song, Union minister Kiren Rijiju said today in a jibe at the main opposition party amid the controversy over the national song.

content: CJP member Sheikh Abdul Hafiz's house was allegedly attacked by BJP workers after he attended the Jantar Mantar protest and raised concerns over the poor infrastructure and mismanagement at a local primary school. His father died after the attack.

title: ‘Students' future at stake’: CJP seeks re-test after alleged glitches in Bombay HC clerk exam
content: alleged technical glitches triggered concerns among candidates . candidates informed him that several computers developed problems soon after they began the test . a majority of candidates were logged out and declared failed within around 10 minutes . dipke questioned the authorities' readiness to conduct online examinations .

title: Punjab Cong faces fresh rift as MP challenges Warring's 'one family, one ticket' rule
content: sukhjinder Singh Randhawa challenged state unit chief amrinder Singh Raja Warring's 'one family, one ticket' stance . he said families could get up to four tickets if their members were capable of winning . "some say I will not give two tickets (to a family) but those who have the capability to win will not only get two but four tickets"

title: 'They were Indian': US cleaning business owner faces scrutiny over racial profiling
content: the north Carolina cleaning business owner faces scrutiny after saying his team did not count Indian callers as potential customers . he wrote on X that he teaches his staff to “profile every client” and said: “They were Indian so we didn't count them as a lead” he also said his team had separated Indian callsers and discussed changing prices to discourage them from using the business .

title: Rahul Gandhi's 'chhatron ki goonj' rally in Pune will be exclusively for girls
content: Congress's Rahul Gandhi said the upcoming rally in Pune will be exclusively for girls . the announcement came as part of his "chhatron ki goonj" meetings targeting the youth . Rahul said the courage with which India's youngsters have stood firm against PM Modi's violent regime is commendable .

title: Parliament at a standstill, protests on streets: The Monsoon session story
content: Parliament’s Monsoon Session played out on two different stages . the session was held from July 20 to august 13 . it produced an unusual contrast: legislation moved forward, but much of the political confrontation played out beyond the floor of the two Houses .

title: 3,000 hectares up in flames: Belgium battles its biggest wildfire on record
content: blaze has already scorched around 3,000 hectares in the high Fens nature reserve . firefighters were concentrating on the advancing front of the fire in eastern eastern belgium . residents evacuated on Saturday were told not to return .

title: Vande Mataram row: Shah takes 'sin' jibe at Sonia; Cong says 'diverting attention'
content: congress stepped up its attack on amit Shah after he alleged that veteran leader Sonia Gandhi committed a sin by stopping national song Vande Mataram midway at the party headquarters on Independence Day . the general secretary said Shah was demanding an apology from the Congress to divert attention from real issues and the government's massive failures .

title: Barrierless tolling makes impact, number of e-notices goes down
content: e-notices fell from 1.7 lakh in may to 1.1 lakh in June and further to 92,240 in July . Mundka toll plaza in Delhi, which went live on may 10, recorded 1.69 lakh . it was rolled out at daulatpura on Delhi-Jaipur highway .

title: Vande Mataram row: Bankim Chandra's kin writes to Sonia Gandhi, seeks apology
content:
The controversy erupted after a video from Congress's Aug 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president Kharge.

NEW DELHI: The row over the full rendition of Vande Mataram at Congress headquarters on Independence Day acquired a Bankim Chandra connection, with BJP MLA Sumitro Chatterjee, a direct descendant of the national song's author, writing to Sonia Gandhi Saturday and demanding an unconditional apology to the country. The controversy erupted after a video from Congress's Aug 15 function showed Sonia gesturing and speaking to party president Mallikarjun Kharge while the full version of Vande Mataram was being sung. In his letter, Chatterjee said the episode had left him with "deep pain, emptiness and anguish", alleging Sonia's "physical gestures" reflected "unease, impatience and repeated attempts to stop" the song. He said the reaction hurt him not only as a citizen but as a direct descendant of Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay. TNN

title: Fleeing drowning scene not proof of culpability, says SC
content: an SC bench said the evidence for an accidental drowning was more plausible than homicide . the two men were convicted by trial court and high court because their friend drowned in a river . they left the spot and went to watch a movie, actions held as evidence of their culpability .

title: CISF officer suspended after woman alleges photo misconduct on Delhi Metro
content: a woman claims a CISF man took her pictures on his mobile phone . the incident happened on yellow line . a video shared on social media shows a few passengers repeatedly asking a police officer to delete the pictures .

title: E coli found in drinking water, rail stations lack basic facilities: CAG
content: bacteriological analysis of drinking water was not carried out at 59 stations in six zones . water samples collected from taps at 49 stations in eight zones during 2022-23 . the findings indicate presence of E coli bacteria in water coolers at eight stations .

title: UP judge sentences 22 to death in 4 months, sparks debate over 'rarest of rare' doctrine
content: the total number of convicts awarded death penalty by him so far stands at 35 . the first set of death sentences in muzaffarnagar came on April 6, when three convictes in the murder of advocate Sameer Saifi were awarded capital punishment . on April 28, four members of a family were sentenced to death .

title: How PM Modi has changed focus of Independence Day speeches
content: the focus of PM Modi's speeches has kept changing since 2014 . he focused on issues such as toilets, bank accounts, poverty and fertiliser shortages . as the country has progressed, so has the theme of his speeches .

title: Lens on Cambridge after Black professor's death amid scrutiny of his credentials
content: the spotlight has now turned to the universities of Cambridge, Durham and Glasgow for allegedly overpromoting Jason Arday . the 41-year-old was found dead at his home on friday, just over a week after resigning from his post as professor of sociology of education at Cambridge .

title: Bangladesh sets tough riders for PM Tarique's visit to India
content: govt: "act expeditiously on extradition of Sheikh Hasina and other criminal fugitives, and help create a 'propitious environment' for him to make the visit" a possible bilateral visit to India is being seen as "surrendering" to opposition forces' call .

title: Navy sailor, wife and 2 kids found dead in Mumbai home; police suspect murder-suicide
content: a 30-year-old sailor, his wife and two children were found dead inside their official residential quarters at Navy Nagar in south Mumbai's Cuffe Parade area . investigators suspect that Puranmal Shambulal Mehra died by suicide . officials stressed that the exact cause of death can only be determined after detailed forensic and post-mortem reports are received .

title: Trump orders cut in US-South Korea drills after Seoul rejects Iran denuclearisation push
content: president Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to “substantially” scale back planned joint military exercises with south Korea . he cited Seoul's refusal to join US efforts to “denuclearise” Iran and his relationship with north Korean leader Kim Jong Un .

title: Never accepted Nalsar invitation, so no question of going: CJI
content: chief justice of india has not accepted invitation to be chief guest at convocation . a section of students opposing his presence at the convocation snowballed after bar Council of India jumped in and ordered blackballing of the graduates before retracting with regret .

title: From hospitals to schools: China expands scrutiny of religious beliefs in Chengdu
content: employees, students asked to disclose beliefs china expands scrutiny of religious affiliation . internal notice circulated by a public hospital in Chengdu said it was conducting a comprehensive survey of employees' religious beliefs . the survey was to cover every employee, including permanent staff, contracted workers and temporary workers .

title: Bengal double murder: 3 arrested over killing of Congress leader, lawyer son
content: anisur Rahman, 50, and his son were shot at and attacked with sharp-edged weapons while returning home . the duo were in their car near Nagadi railway gate in Nakashipara when the assault happened around 9.30pm on Saturday .
